title: Review of the Marangoni sink-escape finding: on fresh seed 92 the escape share is again higher with Marangoni swimming (0.93 vs 0.40, with more bodies caught: 15 and 20) and the gradient on swim distance per cycle is again not positive in the escape arm (-0.17) nor above the removal control (-0.18); Supported
summary: I re-ran the finding's world.py unchanged with labkit (128^2, 320 frames, T=1600) on fresh seed 92 in arms S (mar 40), I (mar 40, caught bodies removed) and S at mar 0, with the finding's DISC_LOG, and applied its fate.py after c00's extract.py (dx 1.0) for the per-track table. Escape: S mar 40 14 of 15 caught bodies escape (0.93), S mar 0 8 of 20 (0.40); arm I removed 1. Persistent splits 31 / 38 / 41, generation 5 / 4 / 7, merge/split 0.51 / 0.36 / 0.21. Selection regression (relative descendants two median cycles after birth): gradient on D at fixed speed and straightness -0.17 [-0.68, -0.00] in S (n=12), -0.18 [-0.36, -0.05] in I (n=23), -0.26 at mar 0.

observations.M: S/seed92/fate.txt: escape share 0.93 (14/15) at mar 40 vs S_mar0/seed92/fate.txt 0.40 (8/20); gradient on D -0.17 (S) vs -0.18 (I): not positive and not above the control, as the finding says

seeds_run.result: pass: escape share higher with swimming (0.93 vs 0.40), D gradient not positive in S (-0.17) and not above I (-0.18)

controls_run.M: I/seed92 (removal arm, same disc stream) and S_mar0/seed92 (Marangoni off)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per arm. My removal-arm gradient (-0.18) is more negative than the finding's (-0.03 on both seeds), so the S-minus-I difference is near zero here rather than negative; the conclusion (no positive selection on distance at this exposure) holds either way. The per-track table comes from c00's extract.py with dx 1.0, which I assume matches the finding's use. The discs caught more bodies on this seed (15-20 vs 3-7).
